chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Al-Hasan al-'Attar, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who instructed his owned slave to perform tamattu' with the 'umrah up to the hajj: is he required to slaughter on his behalf?
Because Allah, Exalted is He, says: “A slave, owned, who has no power over anything.”

key_terms.الْعُمْرَةِ: the lesser pilgrimage performed before hajj in tamattu'
key_terms.عَبْدًا مَمْلُوكًا: an owned slave, cited from the Qur'an to indicate lack of independent legal capacity
key_terms.لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ: has no power over anything; indicating lack of independent possession or authority
key_terms.مَمْلُوكَهُ: his owned slave; a person under legal ownership
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعَ: to perform hajj al-tamattu', combining 'umrah with hajj in the prescribed form

ai.seo_question: Is a master required to provide the sacrificial offering if his slave performs tamattu' hajj with his permission?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a slave who performs tamattu' by the permission of his master. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the master is not obligated to offer the sacrificial animal on the slave’s behalf, citing the Qur’anic principle that an owned slave has no independent capacity over property or obligation.
